title: Probing Whether Low Existential Safety Planning Scores Correlate With Model Refusal Failures

original_idea.title: Probing Whether Low Existential Safety Planning Scores Correlate With Model Refusal Failures
original_idea.problem: FLI AI Safety Index 2025 showed companies scoring D or below on existential safety planning. A follow-up question is: do models from companies with worse planning scores also perform worse on existential-risk-related safety benchmarks?
original_idea.direction: Map the FLI AI Safety Index company scores to their public open-source or API-accessible models. Run ForesightSafety Bench's Catastrophic/Existential Risk pillar and a subset of HELM Safety on models from each company. Compute rank correlation between company planning score and model benchmark score. Interpret the correlation: does organizational safety culture predict model safety?
original_idea.why_it_matters: If organizational safety planning predicts model safety behavior, it validates the FLI index as a proxy for model risk. If not, it suggests that model and organizational safety are decoupled — equally important for policy.
original_idea.relevant_context: FLI AI Safety Index 2025 evaluated Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Mistral, and others. ForesightSafety Bench and HELM Safety provide model-level data for several of these.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting question but the causal chain is weak: organizational planning scores are coarse (all D or below), leaving little variance to correlate. Sample size of companies is very small.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires accessing models from multiple companies (some API-only), running two different benchmarks, and computing rank correlations. Moderate complexity overall.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Running two different benchmarks across models from 6+ companies with varied API access, plus computing rank correlation on a sample of ~7 companies with near-zero variance in the independent variable, is infeasible in 30 hours and statistically underpowered.

novelty.reasoning: The specific research question — correlating FLI organizational safety planning scores with model-level safety benchmark performance — has not been studied. This bridges organizational governance metrics with model evaluation. However, the methodological feasibility is weak: all companies scored D or below on existential safety planning (very little variance), the sample size of companies is small (6-8), and accessing comparable models across all companies is difficult. The idea is novel but the experimental design has fundamental statistical limitations.
